text:
alex: Heads up — console badge shows ~7% of traffic as v2, but routing logs indicate those were served by v1. This is bumping up quota attribution unexpectedly. Anyone else seeing badge/routing divergence?

maria: saw a small drift yesterday morning, thought it was sampling noise. do we have a query to prove mismatch?

alex: quick grep from routing-prod logs: 
```
# sample
ts=2025-06-12T09:12:34Z route=tenant-42 req_id=abc123 header: X-API-Version=v2 served_model=redwood-v1
```
and console shows the same req_id attributed to v2 in the counters.

sam: ugh. could be console aggregation using the header rather than the actual routed model. we had that bug in the fallback window last year.

jeff: can you paste the console query you used? i want to see the counter join keys.

alex: here's the console metric expression (simplified):
```
count_by(version_badge, tenant) = sum(events where header_version == "v2")
```
If header_version was left over from client, but routing replaced it, counters would be wrong.

maria: so console is using header_version (from request) not routed_model. should we switch to routed_model for billing/quotas?

sam: yes — billing should be tied to routed_model (the model actually executed). but be careful: routed_model is only available after the routing decision, so some realtime dashboards that pre-aggregate might still rely on headers.

jeff: what about retroactive correction? if we reattribute last 24h we need to adjust quota billing events and alert customers. prefer to fix going forward and do a reconciliation batch.

alex: proposal: 1) update console counter pipeline to join on routed_model when available, fall back to header_version only for pre-routing telemetry 2) run a reconciliation job for last 48h to recalc attribution and surface top-affected tenants 3) add an audit badge in console saying "attribution mode: routed_model" so customers know.

maria: +1 for audit badge. also add a sampling flag for a shadow path so we can validate without flipping production counters immediately.

sam: implementation notes: routed_model lives in routing_stream with event_type=route_decision. console ingestion collects pre-routing events in fastpath_stream. we need a join window (max 30s) keyed by req_id. sounds doable but needs perf test.

jeff: timeline? infra team oncall is light this afternoon, we can try a small alpha change to console ingestion pipeline and enable on a single tenant cohort.

alex: i'll open a PR with the pipeline change and a toggled flag. plan: feature-flag -> shadow join -> compare diffs -> flip for cohort -> global rollout.

maria: for reconciliation: suggestion to emit a delta CSV with columns tenant, old_attr_count, new_attr_count, diff, pct_change. then ops can review top deltas > 5%.

sam: also add an alert in telemetry: if |old - new| / new > 0.05 for any tenant during shadow run, pause rollout.

console-bot: deploy-checklist created: checklist/6823 "version-attribution-reconciliation" assigned to alex, sam. (link: https://redwood.internal/checklists/6823)

jeff: small UX ask — when we add the audit badge, include tooltip: "Currently attributing usage by routed_model (post-routing). Historical counts may be recalculated during reconciliation." keeps support questions down.

alex: noted. i'll include the copy. also we need to update developer docs: /docs/attribution.md to explain header vs routed_model differences and the reconciliation process.

maria: can we run the reconciliation in dry-run mode and publish a sample report to the tenant owners so they can preview impact?

sam: yes. generate reports and send to tenant owners via support-batch. make sure no billing writes until ops signoff.

jeff: ok. next steps: alex opens PR + feature flag, sam drafts join-window code and perf test, maria coordinates tenant cohort and communication, i'll prep console badge copy and a support FAQ. aim for shadow run tomorrow morning.

alex: thanks. i'll post PR link in-thread when ready. :raised_hands:
